THE THIRD BOOK OF MEQABYAN

CHAPTER 1 — THE WISDOM INSTRUCTIONS OF MEQABYAN

1 These are the words of wisdom that Meqabyan spoke to all the people of the covenant: Hear me, children of Yisra'el. I have fought for the covenant and I have seen YHWH's faithfulness in the battle. Now hear the wisdom He has given me.

2 Do not trust in chariots and do not trust in the strength of the arm. The battle belongs to YHWH and He gives victory to whom He chooses. The one who trusts in weapons will fall when his weapons fail. The one who trusts in YHWH will stand when everything else fails.

3 Teach your children the Torah from their earliest years. Let them learn the covenant before they learn the ways of the world. For the one who learns truth first will recognise falsehood when he meets it. But the one who learns falsehood first will call it truth.

4 Do not oppress the poor and do not take advantage of the widow. For YHWH is the defender of the poor and the protector of the widow and the orphan. What you do to the least of His people, you do to Him.

5 Keep the appointed feasts of YHWH in their proper times. Do not add to them and do not take from them. The appointed times are the covenant calendar and the one who observes them walks in step with the ordering of creation.

6 And above all things: love YHWH your Creator with all your heart and all your soul and all your strength. Let this be the first thing and the last thing and the centre of everything in between. For this is the whole of the covenant.

COMPARATIVE MANUSCRIPT NOTES

[DSS] No DSS parallel. The wisdom instruction genre in Meqabyan Book 3 has conceptual parallels with 4QInstruction but no textual relationship. Both texts represent the ancient Afro-Asiatic pattern of the experienced leader transmitting covenant wisdom to the next generation before his death.

[ORIT GE'EZ] The instruction concerning appointed feasts — keep them in their proper times, add nothing, take nothing away — parallels the calendrical theology of the Orit Ge'ez Yovelim, where the 364-day solar calendar is presented as the divinely ordained covenant calendar. The emphasis on proper timing reflects the ancient Afro-Asiatic understanding that covenant faithfulness includes temporal faithfulness — the right act must be done at the right time.

[MASORETIC VARIANT] The Masoretic Devarim contains the commandment to love YHWH with heart, soul, and strength — the Shema. Meqabyan's closing wisdom instruction reaches the same climactic commandment, confirming that this formulation was understood as the apex of covenant instruction across the full range of the ancient Afro-Asiatic textual tradition.

[CRITICAL NOTE] The instruction not to oppress the poor because YHWH is their defender appears in multiple ancient Afro-Asiatic textual traditions and is one of the most consistent theological statements across the entire corpus — DSS, Orit Ge'ez, and ancient Hebrew texts. The consistency of this moral instruction across traditions that developed independently of each other is evidence of its antiquity and centrality in the original covenantal moral theology.

CHAPTER 2 — THE ESCHATOLOGICAL HOPE AND FINAL DOXOLOGY

1 And Meqabyan spoke of the days that are coming: In the last of the days YHWH will gather His scattered ones from all the corners of the earth. Not one of them will be left among the nations. He will bring them home with great joy.

2 And He will establish them in the land of the covenant and He will dwell among them. There will be no more enemy and no more oppressor. The covenant will be written on their hearts and they will not need to be taught it for they will all know it.

3 And the nations that oppressed them will see their restoration and they will be ashamed. And some of them will come and say: Tell us about your YHWH who has done these things for you. And Yisra'el will tell them and some of them will turn to The Creator.

4 But the enemies who will not turn will be judged. Not by the hand of Yisra'el but by the hand of YHWH Himself. For the vengeance belongs to The Creator and He is perfectly just. His judgment will leave nothing out and nothing will be more or less than it should be.

5 And in that day there will be one people of YHWH and one covenant and one Creator over all. The divisions of the nations will be healed and the scattered ones of Yisra'el will be gathered and the earth will be full of the knowledge of The Creator.

6 Praise be to YHWH who has done all these things and who has preserved His covenant through every generation. Praise be to The Creator who keeps His word and does not abandon the work of His hands. May His name be exalted forever and ever. Amen.

COMPARATIVE MANUSCRIPT NOTES

[DSS] No DSS parallel. The eschatological restoration hope in Meqabyan Book 3 is consistent with the broader Qumran eschatological framework — the gathering of the scattered community, the establishment of covenant, the knowledge of YHWH covering the earth — but the Ge'ez text develops these themes independently within its own narrative tradition.

[ORIT GE'EZ] The final doxology of Meqabyan Book 3 — 'Praise be to YHWH who has done all these things' — places the entire Meqabyan narrative within a liturgical framework. The Ge'ez tradition consistently ends its major compositions with doxology, reflecting the understanding that the purpose of wisdom, covenant faithfulness, and eschatological hope is ultimately the praise of The Creator. This is consistent with the closing theology of the Book of Mysteries (Vol 47 of ACR1).

[MASORETIC VARIANT] The Masoretic Yirmeyahu 31:31-34 contains the promise of a new covenant written on hearts, with no need for external teaching because all will know YHWH. Meqabyan's eschatological vision draws on this same tradition and presents it as the climax of the entire narrative arc: the war, the martyrdom, the faithfulness, the restoration — all culminate in this: the covenant on the heart, YHWH dwelling among His people, and the knowledge of The Creator filling the earth.

[CRITICAL NOTE] The statement that the earth will be "full of the knowledge of The Creator" closing the Third Book of Meqabyan creates a structural parallel with the Book of Mysteries (4Q21) and with Yeshayahu 11:9 in the Orit Ge'ez canon. This closing formula appears at the end of multiple ancient Afro-Asiatic compositions, suggesting it was understood as the definitive statement of the covenantal telos — the ultimate purpose toward which all of creation and covenant history is moving. Its presence in both the DSS tradition and the Orit Ge'ez tradition, independently, is strong evidence of a common ancient source theology.
